title: Prediction Markets Illustrate Probability
markdown:
## What this covers

This fragment records the opening of David Aldous's paper *"Using Prediction Market Data to
Illustrate Undergraduate Probability"*: the title, the abstract, and the first (truncated)
sentence of the introduction. It does not contain enough material to present any of the
probability content itself — no definitions, no statement or proof of the two principles the
paper names, and no data. What follows is only what the source actually gives; nothing here is
reconstructed beyond it.

## What the abstract announces

Aldous frames prediction markets as a rare setting where "results of mathematical probability
theory can be related to events of real-world interest and where theory can be compared to
data" — a combination the abstract says is otherwise hard to find outside games of chance built
on physically symmetric objects (dice, lotteries, roulette wheels). Working from that
motivation, the abstract names two specific results the paper develops:

- the **halftime price principle**
- the **serious candidates principle**

each paired with a real data source: the halftime price principle with baseball data, and the
serious candidates principle with data from the 2012 Republican presidential nomination race.
The source gives only these two names and their data pairings — not the principles'
statements, not their proofs, and not the data itself.

## Where the source breaks off

The introduction opens with the observation that, outside games of chance based on physically
symmetric artifacts, "it is surprisingly difficult to find interesting real-world data that
illustrates undergraduate probability calculations," and the extract stops mid-sentence ("The
majority of examples and exercises in ..."). Everything past that point — the definitions
needed to state the two principles, their derivations, the baseball and primary-race data, and
any exercises built on them — is presumably in the original paper but was not supplied here.

## Sources

- `docs/probability/berkeley/stat205a/aldous-legacy/me134_monthly.md` (library repository) —
  the entirety of this chapter. That file is itself a partial, model-reconstructed extract of
  Aldous's paper *"Using Prediction Market Data to Illustrate Undergraduate Probability"*
  (`me134_monthly.pdf`), converted from a PDF with no text layer; its banner marks it
  `fidelity: reconstructed`, licence `unresolved`, and warns that "every equation is
  unverified" (none appear in the extract itself). Only the title, author, abstract, and the
  first, truncated sentence of Section 1 were available — the rest of the paper, including the
  statement and treatment of the halftime price principle and the serious candidates
  principle, was not supplied and is not covered here.
- No slides, transcript, or exercises were supplied for this chapter.
